slides.title: Vector Spaces: Overview
bullets: Introduction to vector spaces for a first course in linear algebra
Topics: vectors in R^n, vector space axioms, subspaces
Also: span, linear independence and bases
Closes with a short exercise and its solution

slides.title: Vectors in R^n
bullets: A vector in R^n is an ordered list of n real numbers: u = (u1, ..., un)
Addition is done component by component
Scalar multiplication multiplies every component by a real number
The zero vector has every component equal to zero
Vectors in R^2 and R^3 can be drawn as arrows from the origin

equations.explanation: Two vectors are added by adding their corresponding components.
Multiplying a vector by a scalar a multiplies each of its components by a.

slides.notes: The source equations were typeset irregularly; shown here in cleaned form.

slides.title: Vector Space Axioms
bullets: A real vector space is a set V with addition and scalar multiplication satisfying axioms
Addition is commutative and associative
There is a zero vector; every vector has an additive inverse
Scalar multiplication distributes over vector addition and over scalar addition

equations.explanation: Scaling a sum of vectors gives the same result as summing the scaled vectors.

slides.notes: Emphasize the distributive laws as part of the axioms.

slides.title: Examples and Why Axioms Matter
bullets: R^n is a vector space
Polynomials of degree at most n form a vector space
All m by n matrices form a vector space
Any theorem proved from the axioms holds in all these examples at once
slides.notes: Stress the economy of the axiomatic approach.

slides.title: Subspaces
bullets: W ⊆ V is a subspace if it is a vector space with the same operations
Check: W contains the zero vector
Check: W is closed under addition and under scalar multiplication
Example: the line y = 2x in R^2 is a subspace
Non-example: y = 2x + 1 does not contain the zero vector
slides.notes: Three-condition test is enough in practice.

slides.title: Linear Combinations and Span
bullets: A linear combination of v1, ..., vk uses scalar coefficients
The span of a set is the set of all its linear combinations
The span is always a subspace
In R^3, the span of two non-multiple vectors is a plane through the origin

equations.latex: a_1 v_1 + a_2 v_2 + \dots + a_k v_k \quad (4)
equations.explanation: A general linear combination: each vector is scaled by a coefficient and the results are added.

slides.title: Linear Independence
bullets: v1, ..., vk are linearly independent if zero is only obtained with all coefficients zero
Otherwise they are linearly dependent
If dependent, at least one vector is a combination of the others
slides.notes: Independence means no redundancy among the vectors.

slides.title: Basis and Dimension
bullets: A basis of V is a linearly independent set that spans V
Every basis of the same space has the same number of elements
This number is called the dimension
The standard basis of R^n has n vectors, so dim R^n = n
slides.notes: Dimension is well defined because all bases have equal size.

slides.title: Exercise: Are (1, 2) and (3, 6) Independent?
bullets: The second vector is three times the first
So 3(1, 2) - (3, 6) = (0, 0) with coefficients not all zero
Hence the vectors are linearly dependent
They span only a line, not the whole plane

equations.explanation: A nontrivial linear combination equals the zero vector, proving linear dependence.

slides.notes: Let students attempt before revealing the solution.
